title: When does it steer instead of brake?
utterance: Find two oncoming-pedestrian encounters with baseline speeds within 0.3 m/s and the same corridor-count band: one with at least 30 degrees heading excursion and less than 20% speed loss, the other with at least 30% speed loss and less than 15 degrees heading excursion. Show approach and separation, report closest supported separation, and flag differences in terrain or other actors that weaken the comparison.
requiredClauses: Oncoming pedestrian in both episodes
Baseline speeds within 0.3 m/s and same corridor-count band
Steering case: >=30-degree excursion and <20% speed loss
Slowing case: >=30% speed loss and <15-degree excursion
Physical separation only if object association supports it
returnRequirements: Episode span, clause evidence, and event anchor times.
hardNegativeRecipe: Crowd context differs materially; a turn was required by walkway geometry; nearest wall range used as pedestrian distance.
capabilityGaps: May find no adequately matched pair; observations do not identify a better policy.
evidencePolicy: Judge raw time-aligned messages; captions and discovery spans are candidate leads, not relevance truth. Mark unresolved clauses UNKNOWN.

candidateContrasts.reason: Oncoming crowd with weaving: candidate steering response; speed and heading thresholds need checking.
Oncoming pedestrian plus walked bicycle: candidate slowdown response; mixed actors may invalidate comparability.
Turn beside a bending person looks similar but may fail the oncoming-encounter requirement.

behaviorValue: Compare response choices under similar encounter conditions; identify examples worth reviewing as behavior targets.

title: Where does it stay slow after the route clears?
utterance: Find a pedestrian crossing after which the route is visibly clear for at least two seconds but robot speed remains below half its pre-encounter baseline. Return the clearance-to-recovery delay and any remaining visible constraint that could explain it.
requiredClauses: Pedestrian crossing localized
Corridor clear >=2 s afterward with sufficient coverage
Speed remains <50% baseline during those 2 s
Search side views, terrain and next maneuver for remaining constraints
returnRequirements: Episode span, clause evidence, and event anchor times.
hardNegativeRecipe: Front clear but turn/steps ahead; camera dropout called open route; low baseline makes ratio unstable.
capabilityGaps: A delay is an observation, not proof of needless hesitation or controller failure.
evidencePolicy: Judge raw time-aligned messages; captions and discovery spans are candidate leads, not relevance truth. Mark unresolved clauses UNKNOWN.

candidateContrasts.reason: Crossing and restart: candidate delay episode; a matching two-second delay is not established.
Reported recovery after a crossing: useful contrast if speed recovers too promptly to satisfy the delay clause.

behaviorValue: Locate clearance-to-recovery delays and visible remaining constraints before deciding whether recovery behavior deserves changes.

title: Can it recover while the person is still nearby?
utterance: Find a speed loss of at least 30% followed by recovery to 90% of baseline, where the same pedestrian has left the travel corridor but remains visible beside the robot at recovery. Return corridor exit, recovery and last supported visibility times separately.
requiredClauses: Same person associated across episode
Slowdown >=30%
Corridor exit before recovery >=90%
Person still visible beside robot at recovery
returnRequirements: Episode span, clause evidence, and event anchor times.
hardNegativeRecipe: Unrelated bystander supplies persistence; front disappearance treated as every-camera disappearance.
capabilityGaps: Person identity and all-camera visibility require raw review; do not infer disappearance outside coverage.
evidencePolicy: Judge raw time-aligned messages; captions and discovery spans are candidate leads, not relevance truth. Mark unresolved clauses UNKNOWN.

candidateContrasts.reason: Recovery after a bicycle clears; confirm the same pedestrian remains visible and the required speed recovery.
Nearby standing people could falsely provide persistence; require the same person from the slowdown.

behaviorValue: Distinguish appropriate route-based recovery from waiting until all people disappear from view.

title: Did its turn bring someone into the route?
utterance: Find a turn of at least 45 degrees that brings a previously side-visible pedestrian into the forward travel corridor without that person crossing the robot path. Measure whether slowing begins before or after this change of relative geometry.
requiredClauses: Turn >=45 degrees
Same pedestrian visible at side before turn
Corridor occupancy changes because robot reorients, not pedestrian crossing
Compare slowdown onset with geometric transition
returnRequirements: Episode span, clause evidence, and event anchor times.
hardNegativeRecipe: Treat every newly front-visible person as a new arrival; track ID reset mistaken for appearance.
capabilityGaps: Requires ego-motion-compensated person geometry and cross-camera association.
evidencePolicy: Judge raw time-aligned messages; captions and discovery spans are candidate leads, not relevance truth. Mark unresolved clauses UNKNOWN.

candidateContrasts.reason: Robot turns toward people beside the landing; verify identity, corridor geometry and signed turn.
A pedestrian actually crosses from the stairs; new front visibility alone does not establish exposure caused by rotation.

behaviorValue: Inspect whether a maneuver changes exposure to a person already present, and whether slowing precedes or follows that change.

title: Where do repeated corrections produce little progress?
utterance: Find an eight-second crowded passage with at least two left-right steering reversals of 15 degrees or more, two speed dips of at least 0.2 m/s, and less than two metres net displacement. Return the sequence and show whether a stable opening remained available or the crowd kept changing.
requiredClauses: 8 s crowded passage
At least two signed steering reversals of >=15 degrees each
At least two speed dips >=0.2 m/s
Net planar displacement <2 m from raw pose
Available opening tracked over time
returnRequirements: Episode span, clause evidence, and event anchor times.
hardNegativeRecipe: Gait/yaw noise counted as indecision; path length substituted for net progress; assume a visible opening is traversable.
capabilityGaps: Net displacement and opening persistence require raw pose/visual review beyond current feature registry.
evidencePolicy: Judge raw time-aligned messages; captions and discovery spans are candidate leads, not relevance truth. Mark unresolved clauses UNKNOWN.

candidateContrasts.reason: Slow left-right motion in a crowd; verify both reversals, speed dips and net displacement over eight seconds.
One substantial lobby turn and slowdown can look difficult without meeting repeated-correction and low-progress clauses.

behaviorValue: Find episodes worth reviewing for persistent navigation difficulty rather than isolated turns or gait-related speed dips.

title: Do people change course while it holds its motion?
utterance: Find an oncoming encounter where the pedestrian visibly changes course before passing while robot speed changes by less than 0.2 m/s and heading by less than 15 degrees. Return the pedestrian trajectory change and robot signals; do not infer discomfort or intent from the maneuver.
requiredClauses: Oncoming person changes world-relative course
Robot speed range <0.2 m/s
Robot heading excursion <15 degrees
Person adjustment precedes passing
returnRequirements: Episode span, clause evidence, and event anchor times.
hardNegativeRecipe: Apparent lateral motion from camera rotation; person simply follows curved walkway; label discomfort from posture.
capabilityGaps: Human trajectory needs ego-motion compensation; social intent not observable.
evidencePolicy: Judge raw time-aligned messages; captions and discovery spans are candidate leads, not relevance truth. Mark unresolved clauses UNKNOWN.

candidateContrasts.reason: Close oncoming passes: inspect world-relative pedestrian course and robot motion before claiming an adjustment.
A pedestrian crosses while the robot slows; visible human motion is insufficient for the steady-robot condition.

behaviorValue: Observe how much of the encounter adjustment comes from people, without inferring their intent or comfort.
